The flight of millions of Ukrainians after Russia's full invasion in February 2022, Europe's largest refugee movement since the Second World War. Within weeks several million had crossed into Poland, Romania, Hungary, Slovakia and Moldova, and about 8 million more were driven from their homes inside Ukraine.

Most who left were women, children and old people, since men of fighting age were mostly barred from leaving. This time the European Union opened its doors at once. For the first time it switched on its Temporary Protection Directive, which let Ukrainians live, work and send their children to school anywhere in the EU without a long asylum claim.

Poland and Germany hosted the largest numbers. Many people went home as the front settled, but millions stayed abroad for years. Observers noted the contrast with the cold reception given to Syrians and others in the European migrant crisis of 2015.
